facts.text: Emaye Zewditu is a widow living in a small house with a tin roof and a blue wooden door in the city of Jimma.
facts.quote: In the city of Jimma, in the green coffee hills of south-west Ethiopia, a widow named Emaye Zewditu lives in a small house with a tin roof and a blue wooden door.

facts.text: Every morning before sunrise, she spreads fresh green grass on the floor and lights a charcoal stove.
facts.quote: Every morning before sunrise she spreads fresh green grass on the floor and lights a charcoal stove.

facts.text: She washes green coffee beans in a bowl and roasts them on a flat iron pan until they turn dark and shine.
facts.quote: She washes green coffee beans in a bowl and roasts them on a flat iron pan until they turn dark and shine.

facts.text: She carries the smoking pan around the room so the smell fills the house.
facts.quote: She carries the smoking pan around the room so the smell fills the house.

facts.text: She pounds the beans in a wooden mortar and boils them in a black clay jebena.
facts.quote: She pounds the beans in a wooden mortar and boils them in a black clay jebena.

facts.text: She burns frankincense beside the cups.
facts.quote: She burns frankincense beside the cups.

facts.text: In Jimma, coffee is poured three times.
facts.quote: In Jimma, coffee is poured three times.

facts.text: The first cup of coffee is called abol.
facts.quote: The first cup is called abol.

facts.text: The second cup of coffee is called tona.
facts.quote: The second is called tona.

facts.text: The third and last cup is called baraka, which means blessing.
facts.quote: The third and last cup is called baraka, which means blessing.

facts.text: Her only son, Dawit, left Jimma seven years ago on a bus to Addis Ababa to find work.
facts.quote: Her only son, Dawit, left Jimma seven years ago on a bus to Addis Ababa to find work.

facts.text: On the day Dawit left, she told him the third cup would always be his.
facts.quote: On the day he left, she told him the third cup would always be his.

facts.text: Every morning since Dawit left, she sets two small white cups on the tray and a low wooden stool beside the door.
facts.quote: Since then she has set two small white cups on the tray every morning, and a low wooden stool beside the door.

facts.text: She drinks the first cup and the second cup.
facts.quote: She drinks the first cup and the second cup.

facts.text: She pours the third cup for Dawit and leaves it on the tray.
facts.quote: She pours the third cup for Dawit and leaves it on the tray.

facts.text: Every evening when the third cup is cold, she pours it onto the roots of the coffee tree in her yard.
facts.quote: Every evening the third cup is cold, and she pours it onto the roots of the coffee tree in her yard.

facts.text: Dawit works in a tall building in Addis Ababa.
facts.quote: Dawit works in a tall building in Addis Ababa.

facts.text: Dawit calls on holidays and always says he will come next year.
facts.quote: He calls on holidays. He always says he will come next year.

facts.text: One morning in the rainy season, the blue door opens before the coffee has boiled.
facts.quote: One morning in the rainy season, the blue door opens before the coffee has boiled.

facts.text: Dawit arrives carrying a dusty bag and sits on the low stool.
facts.quote: Dawit is standing there with a dusty bag. He sits on the low stool.

facts.text: That morning Dawit pours the third cup himself and gives it to his mother.
facts.quote: That morning he pours the third cup himself, and he gives it to his mother.
